text:
Proposed PyTorch design: aggregate directed counts from training histories only; encode edges as int64 keys `source * (N+1) + target`, sort once, register keys/counts as buffers. Batched lookup uses `torch.searchsorted`, safe index clamping, and equality masks so absent edges return zero; preserve direction and mask padding. This builds on the documented [searchsorted primitive](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.searchsorted.html). Score candidates with `SASRec_score + α*tanh(residual(history,candidate))`, bounding α explicitly. Chunk candidates and, if necessary, history positions; encode each sequence once, reduce edge features immediately, and merge chunk top-k results after masking seen items. Avoid dense catalog-squared matrices. Verify sampled/chunked score agreement, missing-edge handling, directionality, and deterministic tie handling; benchmark peak memory and throughput.

For uncertainty, retain paired per-user hit indicators on identical fixed candidates. Bootstrap paired users within each category, recomputing the four-category macro difference and its 95% interval; [SciPy supports paired resampling](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html). Report category deltas and discordant wins/losses; exact [McNemar tests](https://www.statsmodels.org/dev/generated/statsmodels.stats.contingency_tables.mcnemar.html) provide supplementary comparisons. One changed hit equals 0.5 percentage points/category or 0.125 points macro. These intervals condition on trained models and sampled candidates; they exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability.

Budget-matched ablations: baseline, residual disabled, count-only, learned residual, directed versus symmetrized counts, and bounded versus unbounded residual; hold optimizer, sampling, epochs, and selection opportunities constant. Predeclare comparisons and log every trial. Repeated validation selection causes optimism that ordinary bootstrap intervals cannot remove ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a.html)); reserve confirmation for host-held-out evaluation. Fixed sampled HR@10 supports benchmark-specific conclusions, not full-catalog ranking claims ([Rendle](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263)).
